keyFindings.description: A second run in the same checkout deletes the first run's live out/e2e/nats-store, logs and evidence (lines 111-119) before its own natsd discovers the port is taken, and its EXIT trap removes the store again (line 99). Reproduced at 7d38337be60f in this pod: run 1 started, run 2 (other listener/session ports) exited 1 on bind, out/e2e/nats-store was gone, and run 1 then failed 'listener did not become healthy within 30 seconds' with its listener.log deleted. On main the docker container-name guard (line 113) refused before the rm at line 119, so this is a regression of the deleted collision guard. Fix: take exclusive ownership of out/e2e (e.g. flock on a lock file there, /usr/bin/flock is in the pod) before registering the destructive trap or touching any file, refuse otherwise, and add a same-checkout case to e2e-local.test.sh.

Still says the driver starts a throwaway nats:2.10-alpine container that Docker downloads, and tells the reader to set E2E_NATS_CONTAINER, which the script no longer reads. Documentation made obsolete by this cutover; update it with scripts/README.md.
